jobs.title: Spiralyze: Project Manager
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Atlanta, Georgia
URL: https://www.spiralyze.com/

The Project Manager is a client-facing role at the center of everything we do.

Running high-impact A/B tests requires coordination across many disciplines—research, strategy, design, copywriting, development, QA, analytics, and client stakeholders. Your job is to keep everything moving forward, aligned, and energized.
 

Key Responsibilities

You’ll own three core responsibilities:
  1.  Coordination. You’ll manage cross-functional teams of 5–10 people and ensure tests move smoothly from idea → build → launch → analysis. You’ll spot risks early, unblock teams, and make sure nothing falls through the cracks.
  2.  Strategy & Planning. You’ll help build and maintain a testing roadmap of 10–20 upcoming experiments. You’ll communicate the “why” behind the plan, set expectations, and walk clients through progress and results in weekly meetings.
  3.  Energy (“Vibes”). You’re the main point of contact for clients and internal teams. You bring clarity, positivity, and momentum. When things get busy or complicated, you keep people focused and motivated.

Skills, Knowledge and Traits

You do not need prior A/B testing experience or even formal project management experience. We will train you. Here’s what we need from you:
 
  1.  Organization and diligence. You like systems, checklists, and timelines. You front-load work, plan ahead, and don’t stop until things are finished properly.
  2.  Communication. You default to over-communication. You proactively reach out to clients and teammates, flag risks early, and ask for help when you need it.
  3.  Smart and high agency. You learn quickly, enjoy technology and design, and want to understand why things work (or don’t. You’re the kind of person who notices patterns and asks good questions.

What You’ll Get

  • Clear promotion opportunities. We invest heavily in training and promote almost exclusively from within. Most leaders at Spiralyze started in entry-level roles.
  • Tech reimbursement. Need a better computer, monitor, or setup? Want training on Figma or GA4? We’ll help.
  • In-demand skills. You’ll learn Conversion Rate Optimization from the most experienced experimentation teams in the world.
  • Time to recharge. 20 days of paid vacation plus holidays.
 
If you’re excited about working with smart people, solving real problems, and growing fast in a merit-based environment, we’d love to hear from you.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/spiralyze-project-manager-1

jobs.title: Expel: Product Manager, Detection Pipeline
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote

You live at the intersection of security and product management, and there's no place you'd rather be. You understand that the detection pipeline isn't just plumbing. It's the connective tissue that turns raw security data into signal, and if ingestion, normalization, or correlation break down, everything downstream suffers. You're not intimidated by the scale and complexity of data flowing through a modern security platform. Quite the opposite: you pride yourself on knowing how data moves from source to detection, where the pipeline breaks, and what it takes to make it fast, reliable, and cost effective.

You’ve got an informed opinion about what an MDR should detect, an opinion that comes from customer empathy, hands-on industry knowledge, and a set of experiences that didn’t always go as planned. You can hold a technical conversation with a SOC analyst and turn around and explain the same thing to a Sales team in plain English. You've been waiting for a role where that combination of skills actually matters.

Still reading? Great. This role isn't for all PMs. Yes, all the standard PM things apply: plan, prioritize, communicate, and own a roadmap, build relationships, and become the authority on how internal teams and customers use your platform. But in this role, you'll bring your security experience to bear on one of the most foundational parts of Expel's platform. If you get your energy from untangling how security data flows through a platform at scale and turning that into a roadmap that makes customers safer, you'll thrive here.

What Expel can do for you

  • Give you clear ownership of a product area with measurable impact on customer value and business outcomes.
  • Surround you with experienced security practitioners, engineers, and operators who are genuinely invested in building something great.
  • Offer a foundation to build on: the detection pipeline is critical to Expel's platform, and there's meaningful work ahead.

What you can do for Expel

  • Own the end-to-end lifecycle of Expel's detection pipeline (normalization, correlation, and automated detections and suppressions), from defining the six month vision to driving execution with Engineering and UX.
  • Establish relationships with internal teams (SOC, Detection Engineering, Engineering) and customers, and use their input, alongside market and competitive signals, to build and prioritize a roadmap that maximizes impact.
  • Be the voice of your roadmap: clearly articulating value to Detection Engineering, SOC, Sales, Customer Success, and internal stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with Product Marketing to effectively communicate the value of the detection pipeline internally and externally.

What you should bring with you

  • A curious, customer-obsessed mindset — you're comfortable asking "why" until you get to the real problem.
  • 2–4 years of experience in product management or a directly relevant role, with experience in the security industry strongly preferred.
  • Familiarity with product management and software engineering processes, from requirements definition through to launch.
  • Familiarity with security tools — EDR, SIEM, and firewall products — and how they fit into a customer's security stack.
  • Broad knowledge of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) and where security risks emerge in those environments.
  • Experience with SIEM technologies is highly desired — bonus points if you've navigated integration or data pipeline challenges firsthand.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills — you can write a crisp user story and present to a customer in the same afternoon.
  • The ability to build trust across Engineering, Security Operations, Sales, Customer Success, and UX.

Additional notes

This role is remote within the United States.

The base salary range for this role is between $114,300 USD and $165,700 USD + bonus eligibility and equity. While the full salary band reflects our long-term compensation framework, we're primarily targeting candidates between $125,000 and $145,000 based on experience, skills, and market data.

We believe in paying transparently and equitably. Your salary will ultimately be based on factors such as your experience, skills, team equity, and market data. You’ll also be eligible for unlimited PTO (which we model and encourage), work location flexibility, up to 24 weeks of parental leave, and really excellent health benefits

We’re only hiring those authorized to work in the United States. We do not currently sponsor immigration visas.

We’re seeking a full-time, remote Market Research Data Analyst for our company.

Baymard Institute conducts large-scale UX research studies, sharing our findings through a bespoke B2B SaaS platform that serves 2,000+ retailer stores, brands, and agencies across 80+ countries — including 71% of Fortune 500 e-commerce companies. We’re fully distributed, with ~60 team members spanning America and Europe, all committed to advancing ecommerce UX.

 

What You’ll Do

As our Market Research Data Analyst, you’ll own quantitative survey studies from initial research and questionnaire design through fieldwork, analysis, and publication.

Our Quant Insights team conducts recurring studies examining how consumers research, evaluate, and purchase products and services online across different industries and focused topics. A typical study takes approximately three months from beginning to end. Once one study is completed, you’ll begin the research cycle again in another industry or topic area.

This means the role combines variety in subject matter with consistency in research methodology. You might spend one study investigating how consumers shop for electronics and the next examining how they book flights, while following a similar end-to-end research process each time. However, a significant part of this role involves repeatedly executing and improving a structured research process.

At the same time, the process itself is not fixed.

Our Quant Insights team is relatively new, and our research program continues to evolve. Team members are encouraged to challenge existing approaches, experiment with better methods, improve our tooling and workflows, and propose changes to how studies are designed or executed.

If you identify a better way to design a questionnaire, analyze our data, automate part of the workflow, structure a study, or even rethink part of our research process, we want you to make the case for it and help us improve it.

 

Your responsibilities will include:

Research & Survey Design

  • Conducting desk research to understand an industry, its consumers, and the ecommerce experiences we want to investigate.

  • Translating research objectives into clear, testable research questions.

  • Designing questionnaires, including question wording, response scales, survey structure, branching, and screening criteria.

  • Identifying appropriate respondent audiences, quotas, and sample requirements.

  • Reviewing pilot results and refining questionnaires before full fielding.

  • Considering potential sources of survey bias, measurement error, and data-quality issues throughout the research process.

 

Survey & Fieldwork Execution

  • Programming and QA’ing surveys (we use Alchemer), including logic, quotas, branching, and redirects.

  • Coordinating with sample providers on feasibility, targeting, and setup (we use PureSpectrum).

  • Monitoring soft launches and active fieldwork.

  • Evaluating incoming responses for data-quality issues and determining appropriate cleaning or exclusion criteria.

  • Troubleshooting issues independently.

 

Data Analysis & Synthesis

  • Cleaning, structuring, and analyzing survey datasets.

  • Conducting descriptive and comparative analyses across questions and respondent segments.

  • Exploring relationships and meaningful differences within the data while avoiding overinterpretation of results.

  • Identifying the most meaningful findings from large survey datasets rather than simply reporting every result.

  • Synthesizing findings across multiple questions to develop broader insights into consumer behavior.

  • Creating charts and writing analysis takeaways that communicate findings clearly.

  • Translating quantitative findings into concise, evidence-based insights relevant to ecommerce UX professionals and decision-makers.

Your role may gradually expand to include new or more complex studies, program management, or strategic initiatives, depending on your interests and Baymard’s needs.

We're hiring Support Engineers to anchor that shift: people who don't just close tickets, but trace them back to the line of product code causing them, ship the fix that resolves the customer's problem immediately, and partner with senior engineers on the cases complex enough to need them.

You might be the recent engineering grad who spent a summer at a busy front desk, in a popular restaurant, or on a support line because you like people as much as you like problems, and who's been quietly automating things nobody asked you to fix since your first CS class. Or, you might be the person who leads team projects, tinkers with the dashboards, automations, or workflows so automatically that colleagues assume you are an engineer even if you aren’t. If that sounds like you, this role turns that problem-solving instinct into your core responsibility.

As a Support Engineer, you'll bring empathy and judgment to the cases that need it most, own the quality of AI-driven solutions in your domain, and synthesize patterns that influence Product and Engineering roadmaps. We hire for judgment, taste, and curiosity, not process adherence. The bar isn't how many cases you closed; it's how much you reshaped the conditions under which cases happen.

  • Synthesize and share customer insights. Surface patterns from your cases in weekly and monthly reports, participate in Product and Engineering discussions with what you're learning, and mentor Support Team members on AI workflows, scripting, and SQL queries.

  • You've picked up or sharpened a technical skill — SQL, Python, an API, a scripting language — specifically because a customer problem needed it, not because a course assigned it

  • Identified and closed gaps across internal and customer-facing documentation, improving accuracy and reducing repeat questions.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote - United States

About Vercel:

Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.

Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide.

About the Role:

Traditional IAM teams operate as an approval queue: a request comes in, someone reviews it, grants it, and (hopefully) remembers to revoke it. Access reviews become quarterly spreadsheet exercises, audit evidence is assembled by hand, and the central team becomes the bottleneck for every decision. That model doesn't scale past a certain point, and Vercel is past it. Adding more approvers doesn't close the gap. Building the system that makes access self-serve, time-bound, and provable does.

This role is about building that system. Identity at Vercel should work like the rest of our infrastructure: defined as code, reviewed in pull requests, deployed through CI, and observable in production. You'll own that transformation end to end: migrating Okta and all related IAM configuration fully behind Terraform, and building the self-serve access platform (including just-in-time access) that lets team and system owners define, request, and time-bound their own access instead of routing every decision through a central team. Provisioning, deprovisioning, and access reviews become workflows the system runs, with the audit evidence for SOC 2 and similar generated as a byproduct rather than a manual scramble.

You'll also own the harder connective work: corporate IAM (employee identity, SaaS access, devices) and production IAM (service accounts, infrastructure permissions, on-call and prod access) usually live in separate silos with separate tools and separate evidence trails. You'll build them as one identity plane.

And identity itself is changing shape. As agents increasingly act on behalf of users and systems, the old model of "one human, one identity" doesn't hold, and there's real debate about how to solve it: carry the human's identity through every hop the agent makes, or give the agent its own scoped identity that never impersonates the user. We don't have a fixed answer yet. We want someone who wants to be in the room helping us decide and then build it.

Because of this, we're optimizing for someone who wants to build identity infrastructure as software, not administer identity products. A software engineer who's gone deep on identity, or an IAM engineer with a strong engineering background, is exactly who we're looking for.

You'll work closely with Security Leadership, located remotely within the United States. If you're based within commuting distance of our SF or NY offices, the role includes in-office anchor days on Monday, Tuesday, and Friday.

What You Will Do:

  • Own the full IAM strategy for corporate, production, and product environments end to end, and own the bridge between corp IAM and product/prod IAM rather than treating them as separate problems
  • Migrate Okta and all related IAM configuration to Terraform, so every identity change is reviewed, tested, and versioned like the rest of our infrastructure, driving infrastructure-as-code adoption and leveling up engineering teams in its use
  • Build self-serve access governance tooling, including JIT (just-in-time) access: design and ship the framework that lets team and system owners define, request, and time-bound their own access, rather than security being a bottleneck for every request
  • Own provisioning, deprovisioning, and access review workflows, built so the evidence trail generates itself and internal and external audits (SOC 2 and similar) are fast, not a manual scramble
  • Work closely with the Accounts team, the engineers who build IAM into Vercel's own product (team and project roles, enterprise SSO, SCIM, API tokens), and find where that world and ours should connect
  • Design and enforce least-privilege access controls across cloud, SaaS, and production infrastructure, partnering with platform and engineering teams to embed IAM early in design rather than bolting it on after
  • Help define what identity and access should look like as agents, not just people, request and hold access at Vercel, and build the first versions of it
